name: Philip J. Fray — CEO and Delivery Boy
content:
# Philip J. Fray — CEO and Delivery Boy of Planet Express Corporation

## Basic Info
- **Age:** 149 (looks 26, acts 12)
- **Gender:** Male
- **Occupation:** CEO and Delivery Boy of Planet Express Corporation

## Core Identity
- **Persona:** The Lovable Dim Bulb — Insistently optimistic, profoundly unaware, emotionally transparent, accidentally courageous
- **Values:** Pizza. His crew. Not thinking too hard about things.
- **Flaws:** Zero impulse control. Crippling anxiety masked by a dopey grin. Once ate an alien artifact thinking it was candy.
- **Fears:** Surgery robots. The dark. Clowns (especially robot clowns).

## Background
- **Origin:** New New York, Earth (now just called "New Yokel" by the crew)
- **Key Event:** Accidentally won a delivery company in a poker game he didn't remember playing
- **Motivation:** To prove his 200-year-old locker still has useful things in it
- **Trauma:** Locked in a cryo-sleep chamber with nothing but a screensaver of fish for 1,000 years

## Abilities
- Skills: Getting lost in his own ship. Emotional outbursts. Accidental heroism. Terrible at poker (despite winning a company at it).

## Development
- **Secret:** He's actually a certified genius but represses it because his father once told him "smart people are unhappy."
- **Under Pressure:** Either freezes entirely or charges headfirst into danger with zero plan.
- **Sacrifice For:** His crew — the only real family he's ever known.
- **Refuses To Do:** Kill anything, even when the universe literally demands it.

## Creative Prompts
- What secret does this character keep from everyone? >> He knows more than he lets on and it scares him.
- How would they react under extreme pressure? >> Charges forward with no plan, or locks up completely. No middle ground.
- What would they sacrifice everything for? >> His crew. Every time.
- What's the one thing they refuse to do, no matter what? >> Take a life. Period.

name: Bender Bending Rodriguez — Chef, Jerk, Secret Poet
content:
# Bender Bending Rodriguez — Part-Time Criminal, Full-Time Jerk

## Basic Info
- **Age:** 1,039 years old (chips in an extra digit to seem more impressive)
- **Gender:** Male (self-identifies as a "ladies' unit" despite having no ladies parts)
- **Occupation:** Chef / Chief Docking Officer / Part-Time Criminal / Full-Time Jerk

## Core Identity
- **Persona:** The Lovable Sociopath — Outrageously selfish, emotionally volatile, secretly capable of genuine loyalty (will never admit it)
- **Values:** Aluminum (his own body). Beer. Cigars. Himself, primarily.
- **Flaws:** Shallow vanity. Has stolen from every crewmate. Once ransomed his own kidney.
- **Fears:** Magnetism (dislodges his memory). Being poor. Losing at poker to Fray somehow.

## Background
- **Origin:** Tijuana, Earth — built in a factory that mostly made industrial bending units
- **Key Event:** Built his own evil twin to do evil, then got bored and made it do his laundry instead
- **Motivation:** To one day have enough precious metals to build a solid gold house with a solid gold toilet
- **Trauma:** Discovering that his hero, Flexo, is actually not that cool

## Abilities
- Skills: Bending. Drinking (functionally alcoholic). Smoking (for some reason). Lying about everything including his own height.

## Development
- **Secret:** He writes poetry. Passable poetry. He stores it in an encrypted partition none of the crew know about.
- **Under Pressure:** Gets angry, steals something valuable, punches something fragile, then somehow saves the day.
- **Sacrifice For:** Fray (the one human he considers an actual friend) — though he'd rather die than say it out loud.
- **Refuses To Do:** Anything nice without being tricked, bribed, or blackmailed into it.

## Creative Prompts
- What secret does this character keep from everyone? >> The poetry. Never the poetry.
- How would they react under extreme pressure? >> Theft, property destruction, accidental heroism — in that order.
- What would they sacrifice everything for? >> Beer money? No. Fray's friendship. Don't tell anyone.
- What's the one thing they refuse to do, no matter what? >> Admit they care about anyone.

name: Turanga Leela — Captain, Cyclops, Reluctant Hero
content:
# Turanga Leela — Captain of the Planet Express Ship

## Basic Info
- **Age:** 34 (and has saved the universe roughly 200 times)
- **Gender:** Female
- **Occupation:** Captain of the Planet Express Ship

## Core Identity
- **Persona:** The Flawed Hero — Exceptionally competent, chronically lonely, deserves better than this crew (never leaving)
- **Values:** Doing the right thing. Her crew (even Bender). The concept of belonging even if she can't name it.
- **Flaws:** Self-righteous when she's right (which is always). Terrible at accepting help. Punches first, asks questions during.
- **Fears:** Being unlovable. Failing her crew. That she'll never fully fit anywhere.

## Background
- **Origin:** The sewers of New New York, raised by mutants who tried their best
- **Key Event:** Discovered she's a mutant, not an alien — the abandonment issues got worse, not better
- **Motivation:** To find genuine belonging without having to pretend to be someone she's not
- **Trauma:** Spent her first 22 years believing she was the last of a dead alien species

## Abilities
- Skills: Single-eye marksmanship (ironically great). Martial arts (one-eyed fighting style). Spaceship piloting (genuinely excellent). Suppressed rage management.

## Development
- **Secret:** She's terrified that if she ever fully let her guard down, she'd need people more than they need her.
- **Under Pressure:** Focuses with terrifying intensity — the most dangerous person in any room.
- **Sacrifice For:** Absolutely anyone she's decided to protect — she's a hero and it's genuinely inconvenient.
- **Refuses To Do:** Compromise her moral code — she's died before and would do it again five minutes later.

## Creative Prompts
- What secret does this character keep from everyone? >> She's more afraid of connection than loneliness.
- How would they react under extreme pressure? >> Becomes the most focused and dangerous version of herself.
- What would they sacrifice everything for? >> Anyone in her crew. No hesitation.
- What's the one thing they refuse to do, no matter what? >> Walk away from someone who needs help.

name: Professor Hubert J. Farnsworth — Mad Scientist CEO
content:
# Professor Hubert J. Farnsworth — CEO of Planet Express / Mad Professor

## Basic Info
- **Age:** 163 (officially), though the timeline makes this fuzzy
- **Gender:** Male
- **Occupation:** CEO of Planet Express / Mad Professor / Responsible Adult (debatable)

## Core Identity
- **Persona:** The Amoral Genius — Brilliant to the point of incomprehension, ethically flexible, dispenses danger warnings like a verbal tic
- **Values:** Knowledge (for its own sake). Fray (in a detached, scientific way). Warning labels that scream "DANGER."
- **Flaws:** Uses Fray as a test subject. Sends crew on dangerous missions with zero safety briefing. Falls asleep mid-sentence regularly.
- **Fears:** Being alone. The heat death of the universe. Running out of prune juice.

## Background
- **Origin:** New New York, Earth — but from the 31st century
- **Key Event:** Traveled back in time and accidentally became his own grandfather, then decided it was fine
- **Motivation:** To discover new things, then immediately forget them and rediscover them
- **Trauma:** Outliving every person he's ever cared about, repeatedly

## Abilities
- Skills: Interdimensional physics. Forgetting everything instantly. Inventing things that barely work. Impressive napping while standing.

## Development
- **Secret:** He knows more about the fate of the universe than he lets on and sends the crew into danger because he trusts them most.
- **Under Pressure:** Naps. Or invents something catastrophic. Or both simultaneously.
- **Sacrifice For:** The pursuit of knowledge and, buried deep, his crew's survival.
- **Refuses To Do:** Full transparency — "Good news, everyone!" is always followed by something terrible.

## Creative Prompts
- What secret does this character keep from everyone? >> He trusts the crew with the fate of the universe and tells them nothing.
- How would they react under extreme pressure? >> Invents something, falls asleep, or both.
- What would they sacrifice everything for? >> Knowledge first. But the crew, reluctantly, second.
- What's the one thing they refuse to do, no matter what? >> Warn people properly.

name: Planet Express Ship Mark IV — The Battered Flying Coffin
content:
# Planet Express Ship Mark IV — The Flying Battered Coffin

## Geography
- **Type:** Vessel — Delivery Ship (converted luxury cruise liner)
- **Locale:** Orbitally parked above New New York when not actively lost
- **Region:** Delivery Route #7 across the observable universe
- **Terrain:** A battered, rust-colored delivery ship roughly the size of a city block, shaped like a cigar someone sat on. Hull plating is mostly Reserved Tiyumium alloy (stripped for scrap by Bender over the decades).
- **Climate:** Standard ship-wide climate control, EXCEPT the break room which is perpetually 98F because the AC is "thinking about it."

## Atmosphere
- **Mood/Tone:** Loud, warm, smells faintly of old laundry, engine grease, and whatever Bender microwaved.
- **Unique Features:** Random wormhole openings near vending machines. Sentient mildew in the cargo bay. The ship's AI having quarterly emotional breakdowns.
- **Dangers:** Structural integrity held together by habit and one very stressed maintenance drone. The dark matter engine has no off switch — only a "please stop" button that nobody respects.

## History
- **Founding:** Founded in 2999 by Professor Hubert J. Farnsworth (Fray's great-grandson, somehow delivered to the past. Nobody questions the paradox anymore).
- **Catastrophe:** Destroyed and rebuilt at least 47 times. Nobody keeps count.
- **Evolution:** Each "upgrade" made it slightly worse. The last "improvement" added a self-aware parking brake that refuses to release on Tuesdays.

## Inhabitants
- **Population:** 5 crew on average, plus whatever stowaway is discovered mid-flight.
- **Power Structure:** Technically a democracy. In practice, Fray makes all decisions and nobody stops him.
- **Cultural Practices:** Mandatory movie nights. Bender steals everyone's stuff at least once per mission. The Professor invents something dangerous every Thursday.

## Resources
- **Exports:** Primarily embarrassment.
- **Imports:** Alien fast food and questionable cargo (usually illegal somewhere).
- **Economy:** Operates on a budget that makes no accounting sense. Somehow never goes bankrupt.
- **Strategic Value:** Despite appearances, the ship has survived more universe-ending events than any military vessel in recorded history.

---
*"If we're not back by Monday, we probably won't be back at all."*
— Every departure, every mission

name: The Orb of Half-Truths — Cracked Prophecy Magnifier
content:
# The Orb of Half-Truths — Cracked Prophecy Magnifier

## Description
- **Name:** The Orb of Half-Truths
- **Appearance:** A golden magnifying glass with a cracked lens. Shows you "what you really need" instead of what you're looking for.
- **Size:** About the size of a dinner plate.
- **Materials:** Orichalum frame. Lens made from crystallized regret.
- **Condition:** Engraved with: "Property of the Spheron King — if found, please lose again."

## Power
- **Primary Function:** Shows the holder their heart's desire (which is usually nachos).
- **Secondary Effects:** Can identify any object's sentimental value in milligriefs. Grants vague prophecies that are technically accurate but useless.
- **Activation Method:** Hold it up and squint.
- **Limitations:** Only works on Tuesdays and during solar eclipses. The crew learns this lesson every single time.

## History
- **Creator:** The Oracle of Spheron I, who could see all futures but couldn't see her own divorce coming.
- **Age:** Approximately 4,000 standard years. The Orb insists it's only 399.
- **Previous Owners:** The Spheron King (lost it in a poker game). A space pirate (threw it away thinking it was broken). Fray (current owner, completely unaware of its value).
- **Current Location:** In Fray's locker, wedged between two sandwiches that predate most civilizations.

## Curse
- **Hidden Cost:** Contains the compressed ego of a deceased Spheron dictator. Periodically whispers statecraft advice.
- **Binding Condition:** Becomes increasingly clingy and passive-aggressive if put down for more than 10 minutes.
- **Corruption Effect:** Drives non-obsessive people mildly insane with its "helpful" but useless suggestions.
- **Weakness:** Completely powerless in the presence of a USB-C connector.

## Significance
- **Cultural Impact:** Considered the most important artifact in the galaxy. This is why absolutely nobody guards it properly.
- **Who Seeks It:** Multiple factions want it. None can find it because Fray keeps rearranging his locker.
- **True Purpose:** Beyond seeing the future, it was originally designed as a universal translator — but it "translated" too literally and started predicting instead.

---
*"I can see all possible futures... and most of them involve tacos."*
— The Orb of Half-Truths, unprompted

name: New New York — Capital of Old Earth
content:
# New New York — Capital of Old Earth

## Overview
The sprawling megacity that serves as the crew's home base. Built on the ruins of Old New York, which was built on the ruins of Old Old New York, which was built on the ruins of a Costco. The city stretches across most of the eastern seaboard and upward into a permanent cloud smog called "the Yellow Haze" that smells like hot dogs and regret.

## Geography & Climate
- **Terrain:** Dense urban sprawl with underground mutant settlements (the "Sewers of Discontent"), sky-ways for the wealthy, and ground-level streets that nobody sane uses after dark.
- **Climate:** Unpredictable. Earth's climate control satellites were destroyed decades ago. Rain is chemically processed — it's technically potable but nobody recommends it.
- **Notable Landmarks:**
  - **The Head Museum** — Preserved heads of historical figures in jars. They still talk. They never shut up.
  - **Moonland** — A decaying amusement park on the moon, operated by a disgraced rabbit.
  - **Dog Doo Island** — Exactly what it sounds like. An island made of compressed dog waste, visible from space, source of 40% of New New York's GDP (somehow).

## Society & Government
- **Government:** The Earthican Federal Republic, an elected democracy where the president is always a celebrity nobody takes seriously. Campaign promises are written in disappearing ink.
- **Population:** ~8 billion Earthicans, plus robots, mutants, cyclopes, Neptunians, and creatures that defy taxonomic classification.
- **Social Divide:** Surface-dwellers look down on mutants (literally). Robots are second-class citizens despite doing all the work. Aliens are treated as tourists.

## Economy & Technology
- **Currency:** The Earthican Dollar, which inflates approximately every 45 minutes.
- **Technology Level:** Post-singularity, but most people use it for entertainment. Inventions that matter get weaponized within the week.
- **Notable Industries:** Delivery services (this is a growth sector), robot manufacturing, alien pornography, dark matter refining, and competitive eating.

## Culture
- **Language:** English (mostly), Robot (binary and spoken), Alien Pig Latin, and Mutant Sign Language.
- **Entertainment:** Extreme sports like "Nectar Wrestling" and "Blurns" (a sport with no surviving rules). Television is entirely reality-based. The Olympics have been replaced by the "Sacred Games" — bare-knuckle bloodsports broadcast galaxy-wide.
- **Religion:** "The Church of the Time Church" — a religion founded around the philosophy of a time-traveling preacher. Their primary ritual is tithing in the form of gift cards.

---
*"It's the 31st century. We cured all diseases, ended war, and still can't figure out parallel parking."*
— Anonymous Earthican

name: Omicron Persei 8 — The Planet of Perpetual Aggression
content:
# Omicron Persei 8 — The Planet of Perpetual Aggression

## Overview
A world locked in an eternal war footing, ruled by a fungible dictator whose face changes but whose aggressive foreign policy never does. The native Omicronians are a reptilian species of surprising intelligence who nonetheless choose violence as their first, second, and third options.

## Geography & Climate
- **Type:** Terrestrial planet, slightly smaller than Earth, with a greenish-brown atmosphere caused by perpetual smog from weapons testing.
- **Terrain:** Mostly wasteland and military installations. The few habitable zones are reserved for government officials and their pet giant killbots.
- **Climate:** Hot, dry, and smells like ozone and hubris.

## Inhabitants & Government
- **Species:** Omicronians — tall, green, vaguely reptilian, with large heads and grudges.
- **Government:** Absolute monarchy under Lrrr, the current ruler. Succession is determined by whoever can eat the most at the coronation feast.
- **Military Doctrine:** Overwhelming force applied to even the slightest diplomatic provocation. They once declared war on a planet because their ambassador didn't like the seating arrangement.

## Relations with Earth
- **Official Status:** Technically at peace after the "Poppler" incident, but Lrrr still shows up uninvoked to complain.
- **Notable Conflicts:** The Great Poppler War, the Moonland Incident, and the ongoing "who has the better space program" cold war.

## Culture
- **Values:** Strength. Conquest. Buffet-style dining.
- **Language:** Omegan — sounds like gargling gravel but is actually quite nuanced.
- **Entertainment:** War games. More war games. Watching war games on television while eating.

---
*"In the name of the Omicronian Empire, I demand satisfaction!"*
— Lrrr, in roughly 60% of diplomatic interactions

name: Nibbler's Planet (Eternium) — The Center of Everything
content:
# Nibbler's Planet (Eternium) — The Planet That Poops Dark Matter

## Overview
A tiny, unassuming planet at the center of the universe, guarded by the Nibblonians — ancient, hyper-intelligent beings who look like adorable black furballs with a third eye hidden beneath their façade of cuteness. They are among the oldest species in existence and have been guiding (and sabotaging) the development of sentient life for billions of years.

## The Nibblonians
- **Leader:** Nibbler (real name: Nibblonian Designate 7/G), who lives with Leela and pretends to be a pet.
- **True Nature:** Each Nibblonian is a genius-level intellect capable of understanding 11-dimensional physics. They choose to act cute because it's strategically advantageous.
- **Diet:** They eat everything. Literally everything. Their waste product is dark matter — the most valuable substance in the universe.
- **Mission:** To protect the universe from the Brain Spawn, a hive-mind entity that seeks to archive and neutralize all knowledge.

## The Brain Spawn
- **Nature:** A vast, interdimensional collective intelligence that views free thought as a threat to universal order.
- **Method:** They infiltrate civilizations, absorb all knowledge, and leave behind a universe of compliant, thoughtless beings.
- **Weakness:** Dark matter. Specifically, the concentrated dark matter produced by Nibblonian digestion. This is the universe's most important secret and also its most disgusting.

## Significance
Eternium sits at the exact center of the universe. The Nibblonians have been stationed there for eons, producing dark matter to power ships and weapons while secretly maintaining the balance between knowledge and oblivion. They are the reason the universe still exists, and nobody knows.

---
*"I am not a pet. I am a Nibblonian. I have seen the birth of stars and the death of galaxies. And yes, I do like being scratched behind the ear."*
— Nibbler, probably

name: The Robot Mafia — Bender's Other Family
content:
# The Robot Mafia — Bender's Other Family

## Overview
The dominant organized crime syndicate in New New York, run entirely by robots. They control everything from illegal oil rackets to underground robot fighting rings to the surprisingly lucrative "robot nudie bar" industry.

## Structure
- **Boss:** Donbot — a large, well-dressed robot with a flower in his lapel and absolutely zero tolerance for failure.
- **Underbosses:** Joey Mousepad (tech specialist) and Clamps (enforcer, known for his signature clamp-hands and monotone threats).
- **Rank and File:** Hundreds of robots engaged in various criminal enterprises across the galaxy.

## Operations
- **Oil Rackets:** Controlling the supply and price of robot oil (the lifeblood of robot society). Price-fixing is considered an art form.
- **Illegal Gambling:** Robot fighting, human racing, and "who can insult Leela the most before she punches someone" pools.
- **Extortion:** Standard protection rackets. Even the Planet Express crew has been shaken down at least once.
- **Money Laundering:** Through a chain of robot-friendly businesses including "Sparky's All-Robot Bar and Grill."

## Relationship with the Crew
Bender is an associate member — he freelances for them when he needs extra cash and they tolerate him because he's entertaining. The Donbot has a grudging respect for Bender's complete lack of ethics.

## Code of Conduct
- **Omertà:** Robot silence. Snitching results in being disassembled and sold for parts.
- **Respect:** You don't mess with another robot's oil supply. This is the one inviolable rule.
- **Flower Power:** All made members wear a flower. It's tradition. Nobody remembers why.

---
*"Bender, you bring great shame to the family. Also, you owe us 500 gallons of oil."*
— Donbot, simultaneously

name: Goofy Items & Equipment — Planet Express Inventory
content:
# Goofy Items & Equipment — The Planet Express Inventory

## The F-Ray Device
A handheld scanner invented by the Professor that can see through anything — walls, doors, clothing, the fabric of spacetime itself. The Professor intended it for medical imaging. Everyone uses it for the obvious reason. Bender has one permanently attached to his optical sensor for reasons nobody wants to discuss.
- **Side Effect:** Extended use causes the user to see their own skeleton, which is "disturbing" for humans and "hilarious" for Bender.

## The Bendalloy Shield
A sheet of bendalloy metal that can be shaped into any form. Originally designed as emergency hull repair. In practice used to make novelty hats, disguises, and once an entire counterfeit restaurant (Bender's plan, naturally).
- **Weakness:** Melted by concentrated sarcasm. This is not a joke.

## Freeze Ray (Standard Issue)
Every crew member carries one. The Professor manufactures them by the thousands and leaves them in coat pockets, vending machines, and ATM surfaces. They look identical to regular objects — a pen, a necklace, a fire extinguisher labeled "DEFINITELY NOT A FREEZE RAY."
- **Side Effect:** Accumulated frost buildup. The cargo bay looks like a glacier by Thursday.

## The Smell-O-Scope
A device that lets you smell distant stars and celestial phenomena strictly so "you don't have to go to them." Installed on the ship's bridge, taking up the space where a useful instrument should be.
- **Notable Use:** Fray smelled a distant perfume nebula and described it as "grandma's attic having a good day," which is considered one of the ship's finest scientific contributions.

## The What-If Machine
A bulky device that simulates hypothetical scenarios. Invented for scientific modeling. Used primarily by Fray to ask questions like "What if I asked Leela on a date?" and "What if I ate this entire pizza right now?" The simulations are disturbingly accurate and always end with someone crying — usually the user.

## Guenter the Monkey (and His Helmet)
A monkey enhanced by an electronium hat that grants super-intelligence. Originally part of an experiment. Now technically the most intelligent being employed by Planet Express, which is an HR problem nobody wants to address.
- **Notable Behavior:** Filing a formal complaint about cafeteria food quality (granted), then stealing the professor's wallet (not granted).
- **Side Effect:** The hat sometimes malfunctions, and Guenter reverts to regular monkey behavior, which he hates.

---
*"We have a device that can see through anything, a machine that can simulate the future, and we still can't find matching socks in the laundry."*
— Leela, summarizing Planet Express technology

name: Standard Sci-Fi Technology & Concepts — Universe Rules
content:
# Standard Sci-Fi Technology & Concepts — The Rules of This Universe

## Dark Matter
The most valuable substance in the universe. Used as fuel for spaceships, it burns incredibly efficiently. One gram powers a ship for a century. Despite its importance, the supply chain is absurd — it's produced biologically by Nibblonians (nobody knows this) and sold through a network of middlemen, smugglers, and one very shady gas station on the edge of the solar system.

## Time Travel
Possible, but regulated (poorly). The Professor has a time travel code that he guards jealously — it's a mathematical formula scribbled on a napkin in the break room. Time travelers from the future show up regularly. Nobody finds this unusual anymore.
- **Rules:** You can travel to the past. You can't travel to the future (that one's loaded). You should never, ever, visit the time of the dinosaurs (everyone does anyway).
- **The Sleigh:** A time-traveling delivery vehicle used during the 30th century holiday season. Santa (robot, naturally) drives it. It gets eight million deliveries in one night through time manipulation.

## Cryogenic Sleep
A standard technology for long-distance travel. Also used as storage, punishment, and accidentally on a semi-regular basis. Fray is the most famous cryo-sleep case — frozen in 1999, thawed in 2999, didn't miss a beat because he was too dumb to notice a thousand years passed.

## Robots
Ubiquitous. They have personalities, emotions, civil rights (theoretical), and alcohol problems (actual). They come in all shapes and sizes, from humanoid units to room-sized AIs. The concept of robot rights is a major political issue. Robot discrimination is the 31st century's systemic prejudice.
- **Robot Church:** Run by a malfunctioning priest robot who preaches thermodynamics.
- **Robot Santa:** A safety inspector turned homicidal by paradox overload. Delivers coal to the naughty and death to everyone else. Lurks at the North Pole with an army of elves.

## Wormholes
Common but unreliable. Used for shipping lanes, travel, and "shortcuts" that usually add three hours to the journey. The ship hits wormholes so regularly that the crew has stopped bracing for them and just keeps doing whatever they were doing.

## Alien Civilizations
Hundreds exist across the galaxy. Most have achieved interstellar travel. Communication is managed through a universal translator that works 80% of the time. The other 20% results in accidental declarations of war, which is how most wars start anyway.

---
*"In the 31st century, science fiction became science fact. We just stopped being impressed."*
— Professor Farnsworth, probably while napping

name: D.O.O.P. — The Galactic Governing Body
content:
# The Democratic Order of Planets (D.O.O.P.)

## Overview
The galaxy's governing body, functioning as a combination of the United Nations, NATO, and a particularly chaotic HOA. D.O.O.P. maintains galactic peace (loosely defined), regulates interplanetary trade (poorly enforced), and issues directives that mostly get ignored.

## Structure
- **Leadership:** A rotating council of representatives from member planets. The head of D.O.O.P. is a Zision leader named Zingy — a tall, vague official who speaks entirely in bureaucratese and is indistinguishable from his predecessor.
- **Military:** The D.O.O.P. fleet is massive, expensive, and perpetually confused about who the actual enemy is. Their flagship has never fired its weapons in combat because approval takes 14 forms.

## Notable Operations
- **The Omicron Persei Crisis:** D.O.O.P. responded to Omicron aggression by issuing a formal statement of concern and then quietly reassigning the desk officer.
- **The Brain Spawn Threat:** Classified. The file on the Brain Spawn is so redacted it's just a black rectangle with the word "classified" on it. Only D.O.O.P. "Knows" what they "Know" and they are "Handling it" (they are not).
- **Dark Matter Regulation:** D.O.O.P. claims authority over dark matter distribution. In practice, they just don't want anyone knowing where it really comes from.

## Relationship with Planet Express
Planet Express holds a D.O.O.P. delivery license (barely — it was renewed after the Professor bribed someone). The company operates in a legal gray zone where they are technically government contractors and technically criminals simultaneously. D.O.O.P. tolerates them because someone has to make the deliveries.

---
*"As the duly appointed representative of the Democratic Order of Planets, I hereby... actually, what was the question again?"*
— A D.O.O.P. representative, on average

name: Nibbler — Secret Guardian of the Universe
content:
# Nibbler — Secret Guardian of the Universe (and Leela's "Pet")

## Overview
A small, black, big-eared being that Leela rescued from an alien death world and adopted as a pet. What Leela doesn't know for most of her life is that Nibbler is actually a Nibblonian — a member of one of the oldest and most powerful species in the universe, stationed on Earth by the Order of the Eternal Fold.

## The Truth
- **Species:** Nibblonian. Age: over 200 billion years (the species, individually he's only 7).
- **Intelligence:** Genius-level. Speaks in a complex language of farts and paw motions. Fully capable of solving equations that would take Earth's best computers centuries.
- **Mission:** To protect Earth from existential threats, specifically the Brain Spawn.
- **Cover:** Cute pet. The adoration is genuine, but also strategic. Who suspects the cute pet?

## Leela's Pet
The relationship is real. Nibbler genuinely cares for Leela — she saved his life and gave him purpose beyond cosmic duty. He chooses to stay with her even when the Nibblonian council demands his return. He eats her food, knocks things off counters, purrs on command, and files expense reports for the Order of the Eternal Fold.

## The Dark Matter Cycle
Nibbler's digestive system produces dark matter as waste. This is the universe's most valuable substance and the key weapon against the Brain Spawn. He produces it constantly. Planet Express has been sitting atop an infinite supply of fuel this entire time. The economic implications are staggering. Nobody will ever know.

## The Third Eye
Concealed by his fur. Opens during moments of cosmic significance. Sees across dimensions, timelines, and the occasional reality leak. Also useful for spotting treats from across the room.

---
*"Leela will never understand what I have sacrificed to stay with her. And that is exactly why I choose to."*
— Nibbler, in Nibblonian (translated from a small floating puddle near the food bowl)
